why: The step forks on measurements: whether step 1.20's rows show a gain for turbopackSourceMaps, when production's peak is under 75% so the red line may land, and whether stage 2 is needed at all. Stage 2 (commits 4-5) changes how production is deployed: it builds in CI, uses `vercel deploy --prebuilt`, replaces D530's head-of-main check with a new order guard, and needs Vercel secrets. The brief's own stop_if hands that part to a stronger model. Commits 1-3 are specified file by file with unit tests.
harm_if_wrong: A wrong stage-2 workflow could deploy an older build over a newer one or deploy before a migration is applied. A wrong next-build.mjs could lose next's exit status or never write the stats file, so production builds fail or report nothing.
make_it_cheaper: Split commits 4-5 (stage 2) into a separate step for the stronger model, gated on 'Stage 2 is needed' in docs/build-memory.md; commits 1-3 alone would rate cheap-then-review.
brief_problems: Commit 2 depends on reading step 1.20's rows to decide whether to add turbopackSourceMaps. That is a measured judgement, but a small one.
Commit 3 can only land after production reports a peak under 75%, so it needs a later session and cannot follow commit 2 in the same run.
